data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["HTTP safety/idempotency are end-to-end properties of a single HTTP transaction; log idempotency is a distributed property spanning writer, network, and log","HTTP methods have standardized semantics; log appends are application-defined operations"],"overturn_conditions":["If the log infrastructure is simple (no server-side dedup), factoring is impossible and writer idempotency is strictly required","If the log requires per-operation uniqueness guarantees that only the writer can provide, the factoring argument collapses"],"shared_structure":["Distributed systems distinguish operation-level properties from system-level properties","Idempotency can be factored across components in a distributed system"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_007"],"transfer_claims":["The principle that idempotency can be factored (end-to-end argument) transfers from distributed systems theory","The distinction between 'operation is idempotent' and 'system behaves idempotently' transfers from transaction processing"]},"claim":"An append-only event log does not require its writers to be 'safe' in the RFC 9110 sense, nor does it require them to be idempotent in the strict RFC 9110 sense \u2014 rather, it requires a weaker property: that the *combined system* (writer + log deduplication) produces idempotent behavior. Individual writer operations need not be idempotent if the log infrastructure itself deduplicates. The RFC 9110 definitions apply to HTTP methods on resources, not to distributed message delivery, so the transfer is analogical rather than literal. The log requires the *system-level outcome* to be idempotent, achievable either by idempotent writers or by log-side deduplication.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log performs no server-side deduplication, then writer-level idempotency is strictly required.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If RFC 9110's definitions are taken as transferable to any operation (not just HTTP methods), the 'scoped to HTTP' argument weakens.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log's consistency model requires exactly-once semantics regardless of delivery guarantees, then neither idempotency nor safety suffices \u2014 exactly-once is needed.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110's definitions are scoped to HTTP methods: a safe method has no intended side effects, an idempotent method's repeated invocation yields the same server state as a single invocation. These are properties of HTTP method semantics, not of arbitrary distributed operations. An append-only log under at-least-once delivery needs the end-to-end property that duplicate deliveries do not corrupt the log. This can be achieved by idempotent writers (who attach dedup keys) OR by the log itself (which deduplicates by content hash or operation ID). The log therefore requires idempotent *outcomes* but not necessarily idempotent *writers* per se \u2014 the property can be factored between writer and log.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
